newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro-MP pours cold water on Commission censure.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MP pours cold water on Commission censure.

text.p: Censuring the European Commission over its handling of the mad cow crisis would be harder in practice than most people realised, Italian Socialist Euro-MP Biagio de Giovanni said on Thursday.

"The public is very interested in this subject and wants the European Parliament to do something...I don't know if citizens can understand politics has some complex elements," the new head of the parliament's institutional affairs committee told reporters.
The parliament is due next week to consider several proposals for rapping the Commission over the knuckles.

The choice is between an immediate censure, which has so far failed to win sufficient support among Euro-MPs, a threat of censure at a future date if the Commission fails to improve its internal organisation, and a sound but harmless scolding.
De Giovanni, a professor of political philosophy, said there were at least four obstacles to an effectual motion of censure.
Within the parliament, there was not sufficient support (an absolute majority and two-thirds of the votes cast) for immediate censure.
Even conditional censure would be difficult to achieve because the different political groups were split along national lines.

And even if Euro-MPs could agree, parliament had no power to sanction the Council of Ministers, which was just as responsible for the crisis over bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) as the Commission.
Finally, there was no legal base for censuring the Commission in the European Union treaty, de Giovanni said.
In spite of these restrictions, it was important to point a finger at those responsible in Britain, the Council and the Commission, he said.

He added that the institutional affairs committee would push for the inter-governmental conference on reform of the EU treaty to consider the creation of a truly independent European body to deal with food safety, along the lines of the U.S. Food and Drugs Administration.
In the meantime, he welcomed the Commission's decision, announced on Wednesday, to create a special food safety unit.
The committee also wanted the IGC to consider the possibility of allowing individual commissioners to be censured.
At present, the parliament can only attack the institution as a whole.
